hundred-hills-50km.angle: Two 25km loops return runners to Stonor Park halfway, which makes crew planning simpler than on a point-to-point 50km. The route is still a substantial trail effort: the organiser lists about 1,200m of ascent and a nine-hour overall limit.
hundred-hills-50km.tradeoff: Use the five aid stations and halfway return when planning supplies. Confirm the current qualification and mandatory-kit rules before entering; a looped format does not make the climbing or trail surface easier.

thames-path-100.angle: The published 560m ascent is low for 100 miles, but the 30-hour limit includes intermediate aid-station deadlines. The route runs from Richmond towards Oxford, so start travel and finish collection are separate decisions.
thames-path-100.tradeoff: A Richmond station arrival may help at the start; it does not solve the Oxford finish journey. The organiser flags possible 2027 bridge diversions, so check the final route and the required prior 50-mile result before committing.

north-downs-way-50.angle: This is an approximately 80% trail journey from Farnham to Knockholt Pound, with 5,600ft of published ascent. The 13-hour overall limit also has intermediate cut-offs, so the climb figure matters more than distance alone.
north-downs-way-50.tradeoff: Race HQ and trailhead are different locations around Farnham, while collection parking is near the finish. Plan those handoffs explicitly and check the organiser's marathon qualification condition.

south-downs-way-100.angle: The 100-mile route crosses the South Downs from Matterley Estate to Eastbourne. With 3,800m ascent, an 05:30 start and a 30-hour limit, arrival and overnight pacing are central planning questions.
south-downs-way-100.tradeoff: Twelve aid stations provide support, but the race is point-to-point. Arrange a finish plan independently and check the 100-mile qualification and kit list on the official race page.

south-downs-way-50km.angle: This 50km option uses the South Downs Way for most of its course and has a published 1,150m ascent and nine-hour limit. It is a separate decision from the same event's shorter evening races.
south-downs-way-50km.tradeoff: The start at Matterley Bowl and finish at Queen Elizabeth Country Park are apart. Compare travel arrangements and the four aid stations before treating it as a simple out-and-back day.

autumn-100.angle: Four Thames Path and Ridgeway spurs return to Goring, giving this 100-mile race a central hub rather than a distant finish. The published figures are 1,500m ascent and 28 hours, with intermediate cut-offs.
autumn-100.tradeoff: Repeated returns to Goring may help crew coordination, but 100-mile qualification and the 28-hour clock still govern suitability. Check village access, parking and the organiser's precise aid-station deadlines.

carsington-water-trail-april.angle: The two distances do not share a start: the half marathon leaves the visitor centre at 09:30, while the 10km starts at Millfields at 10:00. Millfields is about 1.3 miles from the shared finish.
carsington-water-trail-april.tradeoff: Choose parking for the distance actually entered, and budget for paid parking. The organiser publishes 200m ascent for the half; do not transfer that figure to the 10km, whose gain and cut-off remain unconfirmed here.

wimbledon-common-half-10k.angle: Gravel and tarmac combine on an undulating common course. The published 60m ascent applies to the 10km only; the half-marathon ascent is not established in this record.
wimbledon-common-half-10k.tradeoff: There is no on-site parking at the playing-field start. The organiser also excludes dogs and says the terrain is unsuitable for buggies and wheelchairs, so this is a poor match if either is essential.

newcastle-half-10k-july.angle: Both distances start and finish at Kingston Park Stadium, with Metro stops nearby. The course uses closed roads and undulating country lanes around Dinnington.
newcastle-half-10k-july.tradeoff: The stadium car-park exit is closed from 08:00 to 12:00. Public transport may avoid that constraint; drivers should check the final road-closure plan and race-pack instructions.

newbury-racecourse-august.angle: A tarmac racecourse circuit makes this a different proposition from a road race that merely starts at a racecourse. The organiser lists 30m ascent for the half marathon, while the 10km has water at roughly 2.5, 5.5 and 7.5km.
newbury-racecourse-august.tradeoff: The station serves the venue and competitor parking is in Car Park 4. Check which distance's start time applies: the half is listed at 09:30, the 10km and 5km at 10:30.

manchester-liverpool-ultra-50.angle: The published 123m ascent is modest for a 50-mile ultra, but it is a point-to-point day from Imperial War Museum North to Liverpool with a 06:00 start and 20:00 finish deadline.
manchester-liverpool-ultra-50.tradeoff: Plan the journey home from a different city. The organiser requires a prior marathon finish and tracker, and does not allow crew access at checkpoint two; check the six-checkpoint schedule before relying on outside support.

ultra-wales-50.angle: This 51-mile mountain and forest race includes Cadair Idris and an organiser figure of 2,898m ascent that is marked provisional. Its 20-hour limit should be considered alongside mountain conditions, not in isolation.
ultra-wales-50.tradeoff: The 06:00 start is at Coed-y-Brenin Visitor Centre, but the finish transfer still needs confirmation. Entry requires age 20 or over, a previous organised marathon finish and a tracker.

ultra-scotland-100.angle: The Southern Upland Way course reaches Galashiels after terrain including Lowther Hill and Minch Moor. The organiser lists 4,611m ascent and 38 hours for this 100-mile point-to-point race.
ultra-scotland-100.tradeoff: Arrange a Galashiels finish transfer before entering, and verify the final start time at St John's Town of Dalry. A prior marathon-distance race is an entry requirement.

queen-elizabeth-olympic-park-february.angle: The 5km and 10km use smooth marked laps in Olympic North Park and share a 09:30 start. The organiser welcomes wheelchair and buggy runners, which is a meaningful distinction from several trail events in the catalogue.
queen-elizabeth-olympic-park-february.tradeoff: Stratford rail links offer a travel option; Westfield parking is paid. The elevation and race cut-off are unconfirmed here, so do not infer a personal-best course from the surface alone.

mens-10k-glasgow.angle: This point-to-point 10km links the Riverside Museum with Glasgow Green via central landmarks. The official 90-minute limit and 09:30 start make the morning journey important.
mens-10k-glasgow.tradeoff: The Sunday subway starts too late to serve the race start, and there is no Riverside Museum parking. Partick rail is about half a mile away; check the final drop-off and baggage instructions.

wrexham-half-marathon.angle: The closed-road half marathon starts at Queensway Stadium and has a three-hour limit tied to road reopening. Water is listed about every 5km, with toilets in the village and near halfway.
wrexham-half-marathon.tradeoff: There is no event parking at the stadium; city-centre parking is around a 15-minute walk away. Leave enough time for that approach and check the final start time and 2027 course map.

newmarket-half-marathon.angle: The Rowley Mile start may suggest a flat racecourse run, but the route moves onto undulating country roads and has a published 210m ascent. The limit is three hours.
newmarket-half-marathon.tradeoff: Free racecourse parking helps arrival, while road closures shape departure. Check the final route and timing if a flat personal-best attempt is your main reason for entering.

swindon-half-marathon.angle: The route heads through Wanborough, Badbury and Medbourne before a downhill finish. Its 170m published ascent means the final descent should not be mistaken for an entirely flat half marathon.
swindon-half-marathon.tradeoff: The free Polo Ground parking is about ten minutes' walk from the start; Coate Water parking has restrictions and charges. The three-hour road-closure limit is a practical entry check.

rugby-half-marathon.angle: This half combines Rugby streets, country roads and a disused railway nature reserve. The published three-hour limit is tied to the road-closure plan.
rugby-half-marathon.tradeoff: Rugby station is about 1.6 miles from the Hart Field start; the limited Rugby Town FC parking is also a walk away. Build that travel time into a 09:00 start rather than treating the station as race HQ.

east-yorkshire-half-10k.angle: The closed-road countryside loop runs through West Newton and New Ellerby. A 30m ascent figure is published for the 10km, while the half-marathon gain remains unconfirmed in this record.
east-yorkshire-half-10k.tradeoff: The half starts at 09:00 and the 10km at 09:45 from Burton Constable Hall. Check distance-specific route and parking directions before assuming the 10km elevation describes the half.
